executiveSummary: Alphen-Chaam's generated 2025 identity, generalized boundary, 10,539-person municipal total, 19 CBS neighbourhoods, six BAG woonplaatsen, 32 TOP10NL settlements, safety-region assignment and signed Dutch road links are coherent with current primary sources. The dedicated 10-preset × 6-checkpoint × 8-service gate passes, including deterministic replay, finite bounds, exact population/demand/delivery reconciliation, causal ledgers, selected-layer invariance, neutral local priority and exact zero-intensity behavior. Recent shared safeguards also work locally: distant flame has finite support, user-facing flood output is a normalized stress proxy, winter cold stress is event-gated, and sustained standing water blocks generic recovery through T+72. Correction is nevertheless required before operational local use. The preset named 'Rhine, Meuse & IJssel high water' assigns Alphen-Chaam an internal 2.668793 depth-like value from a straight centroid-to-line proximity screen, renders 100% inundation stress, places up to 7,298 modeled residents under pressure and accumulates 368,368 event-attributable deprived person-hours by T+72. Official local evidence instead describes a +25 to +5 m NAP sandy landscape draining toward the Mark through the Chaamse, Roode, Strijbeekse, Galderse and other beeks; the regional profile treats primary-river, regional-water, free-draining Bovenmark and extreme-rain mechanisms separately. No current LIWO or waterboard scenario footprint supports the model's direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel assignment. The canonical wildfire ignition is 95.99 km away and therefore produces no direct flame even though provincial and municipal sources explicitly identify Boswachterij Ulvenhout en Chaam as a risky nature area and document local fire-water measures; moving the editable epicentre to the municipality activates flame but still uses no fuel, land cover, wind or access data. The road-derived graph also stops at the Belgian border and is reused for every service. These results are deterministic screening outputs, not hydraulic predictions, utility topology, operator restoration commitments or an emergency-resource inventory.

evidenceSources.title: Regionaal Risicoprofiel 2023–2027
supports: Regional priorities include extreme weather, digital vital-infrastructure disruption and nature fire, alongside infection disease and social unrest.
Flood analysis distinguishes primary Rhine/Meuse/Benedenrivieren systems, regional waters, free-draining Bovenmark and extreme-rain brook/ditch mechanisms.
The southern sloping region is exposed to overflowing beeks and ditches and standing water after extreme rainfall, while primary-dike flood zones are concentrated elsewhere in the region.
Alphen-Chaam is a Belgian-border municipality and regional risk inventory must consider adjacent regions and a cross-border zone.

Administrative geometry does not encode the +25 to +5 m NAP gradient, Mark/beek catchments, soil, infiltration, waterboard split or border-crossing operational systems.

demography.summary: The generated municipal record reproduces official 2025 totals and neighbourhood counts reconcile within expected CBS small-area rounding.
notes: Official/generated population is 10,539, density 113/km², age 65+ is 2,695 or 25.6%, and one-person households total 1,233.
Published neighbourhood population sums to 10,555, 16 above the municipality total or +0.152%; neighbourhood households sum to 4,505 and age 65+ to 2,690.
The local allocator scales published neighbourhood weights back to the exact official municipality population rather than fabricating exact small-area reconciliation.

regionalDetail.summary: All 19 neighbourhoods and 36 declared fields are structurally retained, but field coverage varies and several energy/mobility indicators are wholly unavailable.
notes: Core demographics, density, businesses, buildings, vehicles, access distances and land/water area cover 19/19 neighbourhoods.

Average home value, cars per household and housing-tenure/type percentages cover 16/19; social-benefit fields cover 17/19; district-heating percentage and public charging points cover 0/19 and remain null rather than zero.

Buitengebied Chaam is the largest published neighbourhood at 1,255 residents; sparse rural records have materially longer doctor and supermarket distances, but that does not establish service outage or emergency priority.
The model uses one drainage service despite official evidence that Alphen-Chaam spans two waterboard work areas.

settlements.summary: Six BAG woonplaatsen and 32 BRT settlements are source-valid, non-equivalent spatial concepts whose population attributes must not be forced to the CBS total.
notes: The BRT set contains 25 buurtschappen, one deelkern, three gehuchten and three woonkernen; all generated settlement geometry belongs to GM1723 under the current spatial check.
TOP10NL descriptive settlement populations total 8,935, 15.22% below the CBS municipality total; ontology and reference-date differences make this context rather than a reconciliation target.
Settlement population is not used as current occupancy, evacuation demand or local service allocation.

transport.summary: The five signed Dutch NWB links, no-station result and 37 GTFS stop areas are internally coherent, but the national graph ends at Alphen-Chaam's Belgian border.
notes: Generated routes are A58 to Breda at trunk capacity 260, N639 to Baarle-Nassau and Breda, and N260 to Baarle-Nassau and Gilze en Rijen at regional capacity 150.
The graph has five logical route records but only three Dutch neighbours and no Belgian boundary node, road continuation, mutual-aid or supply edge despite the official border-risk context.
Nominal capacities are synthetic transfer units; GTFS stops are scheduled map context and do not enter mobility, evacuation or emergency-throughput calculations.

emergencyContext.summary: Current primary sources establish local fire, flood, weather, cyber and vital-service relevance, but the simulator contains no verified response-asset inventory or operator restoration topology.
notes: The public context names fire posts Alphen and Chaam, risky forest, local firefighting-water measures and water-management projects; none appears as a typed operational object in the model.

All official neighbourhoods intentionally remain neutral priority 2 with no fabricated hub. That avoids unsupported triage but cannot support facility-specific dispatch, coverage or continuity decisions.
Public sources do not provide current crews/appliances, source/pipe/feeder topology, backup autonomy, household stocks, mutual-aid capacity, switching, restoration priority or repair timelines.

scenarioMatrix.summary: The current build completed all ten canonical presets at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 across all eight essential services without missing or non-finite output.
notes: Reproduction: MUNICIPALITY_AUDIT_CODE=GM1723 pnpm audit:model; one file and two tests passed in 27.08 seconds on 2026-09-02. The current national gate is also recorded green for 342 municipalities × 10 scenarios × 6 checkpoints × 8 services.

At audited checkpoints, severe storm reaches 33.690 mm/h rain, 19.6479 m/s wind and 0.216117 internal inundation stress; pluvial reaches 47.6341 mm/h and 0.520557; river reaches 2.668793; coastal direct flood is zero with wind up to 20.5458 m/s; heat reaches 33.3495 °C and 0.465485 drought stress; winter reaches 27.044 m/s wind, 4.576940 cm/h snow and 0.703437 cold stress; cyber disruption reaches 0.529820; earthquake reaches 0.000784 g; wildfire has zero direct flame with 0.208403 smoke and 0.506571 drought; and compound reaches 81.9786 mm/h rain, 0.536697 internal inundation stress and 0.604534 cyber disruption.
Maximum modeled affected population by preset is severe storm 2,954; pluvial 1,588; river 7,298; coastal 0; heat 1,575; winter 2,628; cyber 2,192; earthquake 0; wildfire 529; and compound 7,946.

T+72 event-attributable deprived person-hours are severe storm 103,910; pluvial 103,502; river 368,368; coastal 47,067; heat 53,187; winter 170,398; cyber 139,102; earthquake 869; wildfire 34,663; and compound 396,605. These are synthetic pressure integrals, not observed human deprivation.

numericalInvariants.summary: Determinism, bounds, exact no-event behavior, local allocation, transfer reconciliation, causal-ledger closure and service-layer invariance pass.
notes: Every service availability stays in [0,1]; event dimensions, demand, delivery, affected population and event-attributable person-hours are non-negative; current severity does not exceed remembered peak severity; and cumulative event-attributable ledgers are monotonic.

At compound T+24, each of all eight service details contains 19 neighbourhood rows summing to official population 10,539 and affected population 6,698. Maximum absolute municipal demand-allocation error is 2.665×10⁻15 and delivery/inbound reconciliation error is 1.776×10⁻15.

For every preset and checkpoint, intensity zero returns exactly zero physical event dimensions, current/peak event severity, affected population and event-attributable person-hours; ambient seasonal temperature remains separate context.
Changing selected public layer does not change physical neighbourhood hazard, municipality hazard, system pressure or affected population.

spatialPlausibility.summary: Finite screens prevent nationwide direct tails, but the major-river footprint contradicts local hydrology and neither pluvial nor wildfire spatial ordering uses local physical layers.
notes: packages/sim-core/src/model.ts computes riverExposure from distance to three simplified line segments with 50 km support. Segment [5.72, 50.84]–[4.5, 51.73] cuts diagonally across southern Brabant and alone produces GM1723's persistent 2.668793 depth-like state without a catchment, waterbody, dike, terrain or hydraulic scenario intersection.

Official evidence instead separates primary-river, Bovenmark/regional-water, local-beek and extreme-rain mechanisms and shows a pronounced local elevation/infiltration gradient. A direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel assignment is unsupported; this does not mean local brook or pluvial risk is absent.

Pluvial and compound neighbourhood ordering is deterministic but seeded, not derived from Chaamse/Galderse beek catchments, elevation, soils, surface sealing, sewer capacity or waterboard project layers.

The canonical wildfire ignition is 95.986 km from the municipality centre and therefore produces zero direct flame. Relocating the editable epicentre to GM1723 gives direct intensity 0.657381 and 620 affected people at T+24, proving configurability, but the spatial field still lacks forest/fuel, wind, access, water and suppression data.

serviceDependencies.summary: All eight declared service cascades execute, but they reuse road-derived transfer links and aggregate local demand rather than operator networks or emergency assets.
notes: System-pressure weights cover power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply and sum to one; service-specific direct and cascade coefficients remain distinct.

Compound minimum service availability reaches 0.133377 and all eight local allocations close, but the values are scenario pressure, not Enexis, Brabant Water, waterboard, telecom, gas, facility or logistics predictions.
The same five NWB municipality-pair links are reused for all services, with transferSemantics=logical-proxy. No physical intermunicipal utility link or Belgian service dependency is represented.

Fire posts, bore wells, the Prinsenbosch source, waterboard catchments and operator context are absent as typed assets; public evidence is insufficient to invent their capacity, fragility, backup or restoration.

causalTrace.summary: Hazard, direct-service, dependency, intervention, network, allocation and reconciliation causes remain deterministic and inspectable with safe proxy labels.
notes: The harness verifies changed-driver explanations, hazard/service/system ledger closure, event-attributable matched-baseline accounting and deterministic repeated frames.

All official neighbourhoods have neutral priority and isHub=false; there are no synthetic local links. Every intermunicipal link identifies logical-proxy semantics rather than claiming a physical utility connection.

A clean headless Chromium run selected GM1723, river T+72 and wildfire T+24 without console or same-origin response errors. The inspector exposed GM1723, Midden- en West-Brabant, official response-geography wording, logical-corridor wording and neighbourhood drilldown.

River output appears as 100% 'inundation stress' rather than an observed metre depth; this presentation correction is important but does not validate the internal forcing that drives service calculations.

recovery72h.summary: The sustained-water and standing-water access guards prevent generic recovery through T+72 in the canonical river and compound runs.
notes: River internal flood stress remains 2.668793 at T+72 and recoveryProgress is exactly zero for power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply.
Compound internal flood stress remains 0.536697 at T+72 and all eight recoveryProgress values are zero. This verifies the shared sustained-flood and generic standing-water repair-block corrections.
The 0.05 internal threshold is a conservative access screen, not a local asset-damage or repair-time calibration; official catchments and actual recession are not ingested.
The first 72 hours do not cover prolonged displacement, environmental effects, reconstruction or long-duration service recovery.

findings.summary: A diagonal major-river proximity segment creates unsupported direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel flooding in Alphen-Chaam.
findings.evidence: The canonical river preset holds internal floodDepthM=2.668793 from T+12 through T+72, renders 100% inundation stress, affects up to 7,298 modeled residents and accumulates 368,368 event-attributable deprived person-hours by T+72. Code inspection traces eligibility to the 50 km distance screen around three hand-coded line segments, including [5.72,50.84]–[4.5,51.73], rather than an official scenario intersection. E11 distinguishes primary-river, regional-water, free-draining Bovenmark and extreme-rain pathways. E13 describes the +25 to +5 m NAP gradient and named local Mark/beek system; E15–E16 confirm catchment-specific local water management. E23 provides the appropriate scenario-layer standard. No reviewed source supports this direct Rhine/Meuse/IJssel footprint.
findings.action: Remove unsupported GM1723 direct eligibility for the named major-river preset as an interim safety screen, while retaining separate local-beek and pluvial relevance. Replace centroid proximity with current versioned LIWO/waterboard scenario intersections carrying mechanism, source, scenario id, probability/context, resolution and coverage. Do not expose metres unless the selected official layer supplies defensible depth semantics.

findings.summary: Neighbourhood rain and compound ordering ignores Alphen-Chaam's actual elevation, brook catchments and split waterboard context.
findings.evidence: Canonical pluvial forcing reaches 47.6341 mm/h and internal flood stress 0.520557; compound reaches 81.9786 mm/h and 0.536697. Local severity is deterministic and service-invariant, but code uses stable seeded variation and aggregate CBS context. E13 identifies a large elevation gradient and the Mark plus five named beeks; E15 and E16 describe current Chaamse/Galdersche catchment work; E17–E18 show that two waterboards cover parts of the municipality. None of those spatial inputs, soils, sewers or road thresholds drives the 19-neighbourhood field.
findings.action: Intersect a licensed current rain-stress or waterboard layer with neighbourhood and transport geometry, explicitly separating Chaamse/Galderse/Strijbeekse and other catchments plus sewer and surface-runoff mechanisms. Keep seeded variation only as a labeled fallback and never describe it as a measured hotspot map.

findings.summary: The default wildfire case misses a documented local risky forest and the editable local case still lacks physical fire controls.
findings.evidence: The canonical ignition is 95.986 km from GM1723 and returns wildfireIntensity=0 at all six checkpoints while smoke reaches 0.208403. A custom ignition at the municipality centre produces direct intensity 0.657381 and 620 affected people at T+24, so the UI can construct a local stress case. E19 explicitly lists Boswachterij Ulvenhout en Chaam as risky based on burnable vegetation, limited bluswater, access and mixed functions; E14 documents two local firefighting-water bore wells; E20 states that weather, fuel, ignition and wind govern fire. The current isotropic radius and smoke field use none of those inputs.
findings.action: Add a clearly named local nature-fire template for the Chaam/Ulvenhout forest complex and use open burnable-land-cover, ignition and wind-aware spread/plume context. Preserve editable epicentres, finite direct support and separate flame/smoke labels; keep access, bluswater and suppression capacity unknown unless approved data supports them.

findings.summary: The logical network terminates at the Belgian border despite official cross-border emergency-risk context.
findings.evidence: GM1723 has five generated links to only Breda, Baarle-Nassau and Gilze en Rijen; there is no Belgian boundary node, road continuation, mutual-aid relation or supply boundary condition. E11 explicitly identifies Alphen-Chaam as a border municipality and requires regional risk analysis to consider adjacent regions and a cross-border zone. E16's Galdersche Beek catchment also borders Flanders. Reusing the Dutch-only graph for mobility, supply and all six other services can falsely imply national closure and redundancy.
findings.action: Add public, typed cross-border road and response-area boundary context for scenario routing and mutual-aid visibility, with unknown operational capacity unless jointly sourced. Keep Belgian transport, utility and response systems out of physical service calculations until compatible authoritative data and agreements are available.

findings.summary: Known public fire-cover and fire-water context is absent from facilities and response state.
findings.evidence: E12 identifies public posts Alphen and Chaam and a Galderseweg attention object; E14 describes two firefighting-water bore wells; E19 establishes a risky local forest. The model has no typed post, water point, forest-access, response-coverage or attention-object node and leaves every official neighbourhood at neutral priority. This is appropriately non-fabricated but cannot answer whether a response resource, route or water point is available.
findings.action: Add source-dated public context nodes and response-area overlays without assigning current crews, appliance availability, capacity, access, backup, priority or response time unless the responsible authority supplies approved aggregate data. Keep operational status explicitly unknown.

findings.summary: All eight essential services share NWB-derived logical corridors rather than physical operator networks.
findings.evidence: The same five Dutch road links carry power, water, drainage, gas, telecom, mobility, facilities and supply in synthetic units. E24 and E25 identify electricity and drinking-water context, while E17–E18 identify waterboard coverage, but none discloses feeders, pipes, valves, pressure zones, switching, backhaul, reserve power, customer criticality or restoration priority. Current output correctly declares transferSemantics=logical-proxy.
findings.action: Retain logical-transfer-proxy wording in every map, legend, inspector, brief and export. Never depict these edges as Enexis, Brabant Water, waterboard, gas or telecom assets; use only operator-authorized, security-reviewed aggregate topology for future physical modeling.

findings.summary: Storm, heat/drought, winter weather and cyber are credible regional directions but exact GM1723 trajectories are uncalibrated.
findings.evidence: E11 prioritizes extreme weather, digital vital-infrastructure disruption and cascading effects; E21 supplies national climate direction. The model's 33.690 mm/h storm rain, 33.3495 °C heat peak, 27.044 m/s winter wind, 4.576940 cm/h snow and 0.529820 cyber disruption are analytic scenario values and deterministic seeds, not time-stamped KNMI observations, forecasts, municipal stress-test grids, operator incident envelopes or threat intelligence.
findings.action: Keep scenario/not-forecast labeling and expose forcing provenance and uncertainty. Use time-stamped KNMI grids, municipal climate layers and approved anonymized operator envelopes before treating exact values or recovery curves as locally calibrated.

findings.summary: The bounded earthquake tail is not an event- or site-calibrated Alphen-Chaam ground-motion estimate.
findings.evidence: The fixed Groningen-centred case reaches only 0.000784 g at the audited checkpoints and zero affected population, but its generic exponential field has no named magnitude, focal mechanism, event grid, local fault/source, soil response or uncertainty. E11 discusses natural fault-related earthquake risk mainly in the eastern safety-region context, while E22 shows that official ShakeMaps combine observations with a Ground Motion Prediction Equation.
findings.action: Treat the result as sensitivity only. Require a named event/source and KNMI-compatible ShakeMap or validated GMPE/site-response grid before presenting exact local g or service consequences as physical evidence.

findings.summary: Shared correction verified locally: intensity zero is an exact no-event counterfactual for every preset and checkpoint.
findings.evidence: Focused replay of all ten canonical presets at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 with intensity=0 returns every physical event dimension, current/peak event severity, affected population and event-attributable deprived person-hours exactly zero for GM1723. Ambient seasonal temperature remains visible without being attributed to the event. This verifies CORR-009 and the event-gated winter correction.
findings.action: Retain the all-preset zero-intensity and before/after-envelope invariants in focused and national release gates.

findings.summary: Shared sustained-flood and standing-water repairs are correctly blocked through T+72.
findings.evidence: River internal flood stress remains 2.668793 at T+72 and compound remains 0.536697; recoveryProgress is exactly zero for all eight services in both cases at T+72. This verifies CORR-004, CORR-011 and CORR-016 locally and avoids substantial generic repair while access is blocked. It does not validate either water footprint or the threshold as local hydraulics.
findings.action: Retain forcing- and standing-water-gated recovery tests, then calibrate recession, access, damage and repair only against named local scenarios and approved operator envelopes.

findings.summary: The live UI presents generic flood output as normalized inundation stress rather than unsupported metres.
findings.evidence: A clean headless browser run selected Alphen-Chaam and river T+72. Inspector and statistics surfaces rendered 100% inundation stress/Flood stress and described the metric as a normalized depth-like scenario proxy, while exact metres are reserved for an explicit sourced layer. Logical-corridor and official response-geography wording also rendered, and municipality-to-CBS-neighbourhood drilldown selected Buitengebied Chaam without console or same-origin response errors. This verifies CORR-017 and CORR-019 presentation behavior.
findings.action: Keep the proxy definition, source fidelity and logical-transfer disclaimer visible in all views and exports; presentation safety must not be used as evidence that the underlying major-river eligibility is correct.

findings.summary: CBS nulls, zeros and small aggregate differences are preserved rather than imputed as observations.
findings.evidence: E02 and the generated context show 19/19 core records, partial 16/19 housing/vehicle-ratio fields, 17/19 benefit fields and 0/19 district-heating/public-charging fields. Published neighbourhood population sums 16 above the official municipal total, while households and age-band counts also reflect independent rounding. The allocator uses exact municipality closure without rewriting source values.
findings.action: Keep null distinct from zero, retain source-edition and coverage metadata, and do not infer undisclosed small-area values or force rounded fields to reconcile.

findings.summary: BAG woonplaatsen and BRT settlements are valid but non-equivalent local geographies.
findings.evidence: E04 yields six BAG woonplaatsen; E05 yields 32 settlements across four types whose descriptive populations total 8,935 versus CBS 10,539. Different geometry, ontology and dates explain the gap and do not establish source corruption or missing residents.
findings.action: Keep source type, edition, geometry method and ontology visible; never substitute BRT descriptive settlement population for CBS municipal population or emergency occupancy.

findings.summary: The current engine closes its deterministic, allocation, counterfactual and proxy-semantics contracts for GM1723.
findings.evidence: The dedicated model gate passes all 480 service-checkpoint cells plus hazard/network/explanation assertions; repeated frames are deterministic; values are finite/bounded; ledgers and local totals close; selected layer cannot alter hazard; all official regions have neutral priority and no synthetic hub/link; and all intermunicipal transfers declare logical-proxy semantics.
findings.action: Retain these invariants in the focused and national gates while correcting the unsupported major-river eligibility and local spatial gaps above.

corrections.validation: As an interim primary-source-backed guard, assert GM1723 direct flood stress is zero for the specifically named Rhine/Meuse/IJssel preset at T+0/6/12/24/48/72 while local pluvial and eligible Mark/Bovenmark/beek contexts remain distinct. The durable fixture must intersect a current LIWO/Brabantse Delta/De Dommel scenario with municipality and neighbourhood geometry and expose mechanism, scenario id, probability/context, resolution and coverage before using physical depth. residualLimitations: The ten canonical presets are deterministic synthetic stress tests, not KNMI forecasts, official event probabilities, warnings, casualty estimates, current incidents or operator outage predictions.

No security-sensitive Enexis, Brabant Water, waterboard, gas, telecom, emergency-service, Belgian or logistics topology, switching, valves, pressure zones, customer priority, backup or restoration data is consumed.

Neighbourhood outputs use aggregate CBS polygons, label points and deterministic allocation; they do not resolve buildings, households, workers, visitors, terrain cells, sewer catchments, roads, forests or actual assets.

No current LIWO, Brabantse Delta, De Dommel or municipal flood/rain-stress raster is ingested, so generic river, pluvial, storm and compound depth-like values are not hydraulically validated local observations.
Zero direct open-coast flooding is plausible for this inland municipality but does not establish safety from primary-river, Mark/Bovenmark, regional-water, brook, drainage or pluvial mechanisms.

Wildfire direct support is finite and the epicentre is editable, but fuels, land cover, ignition probability, barriers, wind-aware spread, smoke concentration, access, bluswater and suppression are not modeled.
The earthquake field lacks magnitude, focal mechanism, event grid, site response and local source characterization; six-hour reporting can miss a short shaking impulse.
Cyber disruption is a dimensionless scenario control without threat actor, affected system, defensive posture, incident evidence, cross-border dependencies or an operator recovery playbook.

Generic preparedness, response delay, backup, generator, repair capacity, network capacity and mutual-aid controls are scenario assumptions, not verified local inventories, contracts, dispatch times or commitments.
Affected population is a thresholded people-equivalent indicator, not persons known to be injured, evacuated or deprived; zero can coexist with non-zero hazard and service pressure.
Cumulative deprived person-hours are event-attributable model pressure integrals, not observed deprivation, economic loss or welfare impact.
CBS neighbourhood counts and percentages are rounded and field availability varies; close aggregate differences must not be forced to exact equality where official semantics do not support it.
BAG, BRT, CBS, NWB, ProRail and GTFS products use different ontologies, geometry generalisation, boundaries, update cycles and reference dates.
GTFS stop areas and ProRail station geometry are display context only and do not encode vehicles, ridership, operating condition, accessible capacity, evacuation throughput or current disruption.
The first-72-hour horizon excludes prolonged displacement, environmental and health effects, reconstruction, economic loss, cross-border crisis coordination and long-duration recovery.

The regional profile includes infection disease, social unrest, dangerous goods, industrial, crowd, health and other emergencies outside the ten canonical presets; scenario coverage is not a complete local risk assessment.
